fixes.explanation: True, baker. Luke 23:25 says, "As they had requested, he released the one imprisoned for insurrection and murder…" That's Barabbas. They had cried out, "Release Barabbas to us!" (Luke 23:18). The same verse says Pilate "handed Jesus over to their will."

Right, baker. The chief priests and scribes do stand there, but Luke 23:10 says they were "…vehemently accusing Him." Quiet isn't the word the verse uses. Meanwhile, Herod is questioning Jesus at great length (Luke 23:9).

Yes, baker. Pilate says, "Therefore I will punish Him and release Him." (Luke 23:16). Release is the word he lands on. He says it again in Luke 23:22: "So after I punish Him, I will release Him." Twice is still fewer times than I've said "one more minute" at my oven.
